hints: Notice the $0.15 \text{ C}$ that passes is carried by $N$ free electrons in a cylinder of wire of length $L$ equal to their average displacement.
Connect that cylinder volume $AL$ to charge using number density $n = 8.5 \times 10^{28} \text{ m}^{-3}$ and elementary charge $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ with $Q = nALe$.
First calculate the cross-sectional area from diameter $0.42 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ using $r = d/2$ and $A = \pi r^2$, then rearrange to $L = Q/(nAe)$ and substitute.
walkthrough: Identify the volume swept by the drifting electrons as $V = AL$, where $L$ is the required average displacement along the wire.
State the charge relation: number of electrons is $N = nV = nAL$, so charge moved is $Q = Ne = nALe$.
Calculate the wire area: $r = 0.42 \times 10^{-3}/2 = 0.21 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, so $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(0.21 \times 10^{-3})^2 \approx 1.39 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$.
Rearrange for displacement: $L = Q/(nAe)$ and substitute $Q = 0.15 \text{ C}$, $n = 8.5 \times 10^{28} \text{ m}^{-3}$ and $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Evaluate: $L = 0.15/(8.5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.39 \times 10^{-7} \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19}) \approx 8.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$, with units of length as required. This is option C.
